name: Shimei
overview: Shimei was a male Levite who served as an officer in charge of the consecrated things, indicating a role of responsibility within the religious duties of Israel. His service is noted in 2 Chronicles 31:12, highlighting his involvement in the administration of sacred offerings and items. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimei means 'YHWH has heard' or 'famous,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's attentiveness. This proper name emphasizes a connection to God's awareness and reputation, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:12.
familyAndRelationships: Shimei is identified as a descendant of Levi, placing him within the priestly tribe entrusted with temple service. He is also noted to have a brother named Conaniah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:13. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Shimei's role as an officer overseeing the consecrated things underscores the importance of faithful stewardship in the worship of God during the post-exilic period. His Levitical lineage and specific duties illustrate the organized structure God established for temple service. Through his service, Shimei contributed to the proper administration of sacred offerings, reflecting the biblical emphasis on holiness and order in worship.
